column3: Every federal student loan as one (balances added, the APR weighted). AGI = gross - before-tax saving - the student loan interest deduction. Standard: 10 years (the tiered plan by balance for a loan first disbursed July 2026 or later). IBR: 10% (15% before July 2014) of AGI over 150% of the poverty guideline / 12, never over the 10-year payment, forgiven after 20 (25) years less the payments made. RAP: 1% to 10% of the whole AGI by band / 12, less $50 a dependent, at least $10; interest a payment leaves is waived, and a payment that takes less than $50 off the principal takes up to $50 more (the lesser of $50 and the part that went to interest); forgiven after 30 years. With PSLF (Yes or Not sure): forgiven, tax-free, after 120 qualifying payments less those made. Each plan walked month by month (simple interest: unpaid interest waits beside the principal). Tax on IBR or RAP forgiveness: the federal tax it adds, in today's dollars against today's brackets. Income held where it is today.

column2: Ranges on the key outputs: low, likely and high
column3: The corner method (docs/engines/ranges.md): likely is the plan as entered, the number every screen shows. Then the whole plan is run again with each uncertain input at its low and at its high, the rest as entered. An input's swing on an output is the gap between its two runs; the swings combine as the root of the sum of their squares, one side at a time (inputs taken as independent). The gut number and the Budget lines are one input (they move together); each income, balance, value and APR is its own. How far an input moves comes from its level and kind (Assumptions: RangeBalance*, RangeSpend*, RangeIncome*, RangeVariable*, RangeApr*, RoughBalanceShare, AprGuessSwing); a typical amount not answered yet moves TypicalLow to TypicalHigh. Outputs: the FI date, the debt-free date, emergency fund months, the monthly surplus, net worth (low, likely, high each) and the FOO step (the earliest and latest step any one input reaches). A date that never comes at an end is blank there (or later). Shown only when the inputs below Know it move it more than the materiality (MaterialHours at the real hourly wage, never under MaterialFloor; a surplus counts a year; a date at least RangeMinMonths, its months valued at a month of spending; emergency fund months at least RangeMinEfMonths). The value counts the outputs wide enough to show.

column2: The plan from an age: typical for the age until answered
column3: Batch 46 (the age-only start). From an age alone (plus the state and Solo or Couple when About you has them) each blank core input is filled by its typical amount for the age (M9E): pay (the Census median household income shaped like CE spending by age, gross, then M12's tax), spending all in (CE, the one-person row scaled by the age band's ratio to all ages, QUESTIONS 336; NY and NJ by their price parity), checking and savings (the SCF median shaped like spending), invested (the SCF retirement median among holders shaped like net worth by age) and card balances (the SCF median among carriers). A typical amount is all households' 25th, middle and 75th, those with none counted as $0 (a 44.7% share carrying a card balance means $0 at the middle). The filled household is a copy, never saved and never counted toward the Picture %. The ranges method (M9R) then runs the plan again with each typical amount at its low and its high: pay and spending move together while both are typical, and the share of pay spent moves PriorSpendShare either way; once one is answered the other moves PriorSpendShare. Outputs: the FI date, the debt-free date, emergency fund months and the monthly surplus, each low, likely and high. A likely FI date that never comes still gives the soonest end (or later). The value counts the core inputs still typical.

column2: What a lender sees: a mortgage lender, a landlord and a card issuer
column3: Each income row read three ways (js/math/lender.js). A paycheck counts at its gross (card tips are on it); cash tips only when reported. Self-employment (1099, a business, a side hustle, a Platform row) counts from the returns filed, net of costs written off: two returns averaged but never more than the latest (Fannie Mae B3-3.1-01 on a declining trend; FHA 4000.1 the lesser of the averages); one return, a mortgage lender waits for the second and a landlord reads it; none, nothing. Unemployment does not count for a mortgage (seasonal work only); a benefit counts when it runs LenderBenefitYears (mortgage) or LenderLeaseMonths (landlord); Rental as typed, its loan netted; gifts in neither. Debts at the payment on the credit report: a card at its minimum (M30), a student loan with none at LenderStudentPct of the balance, no family loans. The mortgage read is total DTI against LenderBack, LenderFhaBack, LenderBackStrong and LenderBackDu, and the home payment the usual lines clear (min of LenderFront x income and LenderBack x income less other debts), as a loan at LenderMortgageRate over LenderMortgageYears after LenderTaxInsShare for taxes and insurance. The landlord read is gross a month over the rent against LenderRentTimes (LenderRentYearNyc / 12 in NYC). The card read is utilization against UtilHigh and UtilBest, with what to pay before the statement closes. The gap is earned less what a mortgage lender counts, a month, and the home loan and rent it rules out. Each move is the reading run again with one change (reporting tips, filing the next return in full, paying off the debt with the biggest payment for its balance); the two that move each read most are shown.

column2: Bank fire drill: days the reachable money covers the must-pay bills
column3: Pick a bank account (default: where the largest paycheck lands, its Lands in or its owner's checking). If it froze today: the calendar's next FireDrillDays (30) days, each paycheck by its Lands in and each bill by its Paid with (else its owner's checking); out of reach = its balance + accounts known at the same bank (Institutions, or Same bank tapped on the drill) + the pay landing there. Still reachable = other bank accounts (not Purpose: Taxes, listed apart) + cash on hand; card room = limit - balance on cards not at that bank (no limit: none). Must-pay a month = the Budget lines in housing, utilities and phone, food, getting to work, health and childcare, plus the mortgage and car payments, plus every other debt's minimum (M30); with only a gut number, the gut number (less the other debts' payments in it) plus the minimums. Days = floor(reachable / (must-pay x 12 / 365)); with the card = floor(min((reachable + room) / (must-pay x 12 / 365), reachable / ((housing + minimums) x 12 / 365))). The order (Bill_order: housing, utilities, food, getting to work, health, minimums, taxes, the rest): every outflow in the window not on a working card, a debt split into its minimum and the rest, paid in that order from the reachable cash and pay landing elsewhere, then the card room for a tier a card can pay. Stranded: a platform's held balance = net a month x 12 / 365 x hold days.

column2: Ask me next and the certainty meter
column3: Built on the ranges (M9R). The certainty meter: for each key output (the FI date, the debt-free date, emergency fund months, the monthly surplus, net worth), 1 minus its width over the width it would have with every input on file read as a guess (the stand-in for age-only), clamped 0 to 1; the meter is their weighted average (Assumptions: CertaintyWeight*). A date that could run on and never come counts CertaintyOpenMonths wide. Ask me next: the Picture %'s next small things come first when the plan cannot run without one (nothing typed yet); then each input below Know it is read at the level its answer reaches (the gut number read off a statement or an app: Estimate; a statements total built from the lines, and any other number: Know it), that one input is run again, and each key output's drop in width over its all-guess width is added up by weight, plus CertaintyWeightFoo when the answer settles the FOO step. Score = that over the seconds the question takes (AskSecondsNumber for a number already given, AskSecondsLookup for one read off an app or statement, AskSecondsBuild for the lines). On a near tie (2%) the input behind These are big deals (M56) goes first, then the next small things order. Skipped: Will get it (homework) and Not now. The value is the meter; the parts are the question and the runner-up.

column2: The benefits cliff: the lines a raise crosses and what the household keeps
column3: js/math/cliff.js. The household size is you, a partner when Solo or couple says Couple, and the children (Dependents or Kids ages); its income a year is every income row but gifts, earned (paychecks with cash tips, self-employment) or not, and MAGI is that less pre-tax money and half the SE tax. Each line is a multiple of the poverty line (Poverty_base + Poverty_perPerson x (size - 1)) or a table: SNAP's gross line a month (SNAP_limits at 130%; New York SNAP_nyEarned with earnings, SNAP_nyCare with child care paid out of pocket or someone 60 or older; outside New York the net line too), its benefit (the most for the size less SNAP_benefitShare of net income: gross less SNAP_earnedShare of earnings, the standard deduction and the shelter costs over SNAP_shelterShare of what is left, capped at SNAP_shelterCap; rent plus SNAP_suaNyc or SNAP_suaRest in New York; at least SNAP_minimum for SNAP_minimumUpTo people); health coverage as one chain (Medicaid to Medicaid_adults in an expansion state, the Essential Plan to NY_essential in New York at NY_essentialPremium, then the benchmark plan from ACA_benchmark less the ACA_applicable share of MAGI, none over ACA_cliff, none under ACA_floor); New York children (NY_kidsMedicaid, NY_infantMedicaid, NY_chpFree, then NY_chpBands, full price over 400% not priced); the EITC (EITC_2026, phased in at the full credit over its earnings and out from the threshold to the end, plus EITC_nyShare in New York; none with no children under EITC_ageMin or over EITC_ageMax). A raise is a W-2 paycheck added to the household: kept = the raise less the household tax it adds (M12); each program tapped Getting it (and still under its line) is read again at the higher income, and the net is kept less what each loses. The break-even is the smallest raise at or above the one tested, in $100 steps, that leaves the net at or above zero.

column2: The year-by-year projection: months to FI on the full plan
column3: Batch 50, the core of docs/engines/projection.md (js/math/projection.js). The household is walked a month at a time from this month to Plan to age (the first 12 months reported month by month, then year by year): each person's age; each income row by its person (W-2, side work, self-employment and platform pay stop at the stop age, Retire by or the FI age, else 65; rent, family help and benefits keep going; unemployment ends on its date); a raise (ProjectionRaise) or a job that stops is taxed by SLAM's tax function as it is (M10); the 401(k), the HSA and the match held to the limit for that person's age in that calendar year (catch-ups from the year they turn 50, 55 for the HSA, 60 to 63 the larger one; the 415(c) total), pay over a limit comes back after the marginal rate; the surplus (M27, with the known changes ahead) routed by the FOO flow (M79): FOO step 1 and big e to cash, heavy debt through the one debt plan (M34), then Tax-Free Growth (Roth IRA and HSA room each calendar year) and the rest to taxable; each account by tax type (cash, taxable, pretax, Roth, HSA, 529 and goal money apart) grows at the real return a month ((1 + return)^(1/12), then the month's money, as M53); once every debt is gone its payments come back to the month; a short month while working is drawn from cash and is never borrowed; once work stops, cash then taxable, Roth, HSA and pretax (before 59½ flagged). FI is the first month invested reaches the FI number (M50).

A row is shared when its Owner is Joint (everyone on this row) or it is a bill split with them. Shared among: the adults ticked, blank is everyone. Split how: Equal is 1 / the people it is shared among; Percent is the percent typed for each, the people with none typed sharing what is left equally; By income is their take-home over the take-home of everyone on the row (equal while none is known); blank follows Shared bills split on About you. The household's books (and its view, Everyone) count every row whole, a shared bill once (less the roommates' part when roommates outside the plan share it); one adult's view counts their own rows and their part of the shared ones, and a row shared among others is not in it. column2: Shift P&L: what a shift really pays an hour
column3: Batch 51 (Phase 5, real lives wave 2). For each income row with shifts a week, a shift: the gross (pay or the paycheck before tax, card tips, cash tips) less the house or stage fee, the tip-out and the tax (whatever lies between the gross and the row's own take-home a shift, M12 over shifts a month) = the take-home a shift (Tips and shifts). Less getting there (a ride or fare each way x the ways, both unless One way is tapped; or the miles there and back x MileageRate), childcare (sitter hours x the sitter's rate) and outfits and gear (what they cost / the shifts they last) = what the shift leaves. Real hourly = that / every hour a shift takes (getting ready + travel + the shift + winding down); on the clock = take-home a shift / the shift's hours; beside M17 the hourly value. Rows ranked by real hourly. A view of one shift: spending already holds these costs, so the surplus does not change. A row kept private for the audience is left out of the list (Includes amounts kept private).
